analysis: This PR is documentation-only: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/watchdog-isolated-crash-restart.md, lines 1-3) and one new runtime-constants row plus a date bump in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 3 and line 2016). No executable source, authorization, attestation, encryption or data-handling code is in the supplied evidence. The documented behavior change is that the watchdog restarts an isolated crash on its next 60 s check (1-2 min) instead of after 6-7 min. A restart that would continue a crash-loop chain (crash within 15 min of the last restart) still waits the 300 s grace, so the crash-loop guard (threshold 3) and rollback are described as unchanged. Relevant threat: T-043 (watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable binary; TB-003), plus A-018 availability and the T-053/T-057 restart/authorization lifecycle. The docs say the guard and rollback are unchanged, but the actual Swift change to WatchdogDecision.swift / WatchdogPolicy.graceSeconds is not supplied, so I cannot confirm the claim. The next pass should check that code for three things: whether faster restarts weaken crash-loop counting, how the restart-time and 15-minute chain window are persisted in watchdog-state.json and whether the operator can tamper with them, and whether restart after a crash still goes through the normal authorization and attestation path rather than reusing stale grants. The earlier CLI reference text on logout, drain, add-on and cache storage is unchanged context, not modified here. No concrete security regression is identifiable from the documentation alone.
